Unofficial until approved by the
  Alhambra City Council

  MINUTES
  Adjourned Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  December 9, 2024
  4:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 4:12 p.m., on Monday, December 9, 2024, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Deputy Director of Public Works and Utilities
Ramos, Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services
LohGuan, Director of Human Resources Ko, Battalion Chief Brown, Economic Development Specialist
Chew, Manager Analyst Alvarez

FLAG SALUTE:  Vice Mayor Lee

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

PRESENTATION

1.  WRENSMOOR CASTLE CONTINUED OPERATION – F2M24-33, M2M24-215

  Director of Community Development HO delivered a staff report. On September 23, 2024, the
  Short-Term Rental ordinance was approved, establishing regulations on short term rentals
  including the prohibition of parties and commercial events on properties. Subsequently, at the
  October 28, 2024 Council meeting, representatives from Wrensmoor Castle raised concerns
  about how the new regulations would negatively impact their business and asked the City to
  make an exemption for their property to allow for continued operation. The City Council
  requested this item be agendized to discuss further. Wrensmoor Castle is located at 1700
  Grand View Dr. and has been sometimes referred to as the Phil Spector House. Following the
  sale of the property, Wrensmoor leased the property in March 2022. The facility has operated
  as a short-term rental but has also allowed short term rentals to hold weddings. In addition,
  the facility has been used by film companies for production. Currently, Wrensmoor is located
  on a residentially zoned property in a residential neighborhood; the operation of catered
  weddings and special events and filming are considered commercial and inconsistent with
  residential zoning. To allow Wrensmoor to continue operating, the operation of the facility
  must be allowed in the residential zone, and regulations would need to be developed to ensure
  1
12-9-24
   the continued operation of Wrensmoor would not negatively impact the neighborhood. Should
  the City Council desire to allow Wrensmoor to continue to operate, the City could require a
  conditional use permit for short term rental uses that have 6+ rooms; this would include stays,
  events, and routine filming and one of the conditions of the approval would be the use must
  operate consistent with the requirements of a special short term rental permit approved by the
  City Council.

  Public Comment:
  1) Kristopher GAY, 1910 Alta Vista Dr., spoke regarding the negative impact Wrensmoor has had
  on the neighborhood, stated that he felt Ms. Culver was not a good faith actor, that she had
  mischaracterized Wrensmoor as an AirBnB, that her business was in violation of the zoning
  code, and that she denied several impacts to the surrounding area. He urged Council to not
  allow Wrensmoor to continue operating.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the potential of the property but added
  that it must work for the neighborhood.

  3) Delilah NGA DO, 1910 Alta Vista Dr., spoke against Wrensmoor and discussed the negative
  impact on the neighborhood including increased traffic, deliveries, and safety threats. She
  stated that she did not choose to live near a wedding event venue and that this was not a
  commercial district.

  4) Denise DELGADO, 1800 Alta Vista Dr., spoke against Wrensmoor and discussed the negative
  impact on the neighborhood including increased traffic and street parking. She stated that this
  was a residential neighborhood and that it did not work with this commercial use.

  5) Alan FRIEDMAN, 1717 Alta Vista Dr., spoke against Wrensmoor and discussed the negative
  impact on the neighborhood including noise, parking, and the impact of home resale in the
  neighborhood.

  6) Cordelia CULVER, 1700 Grand View Ave., the operator of Wrensmoor Castle, thanked Council
  for considering the amendment. She stated that she felt they had changed their rules to correct
  past incidents and expressed her hope that they could address the neighbors’ concerns. She
  also stated that she believed the business did have a value to the community in preserving an
  historic property and using it to attract people to Alhambra.

  7) Jose GARCIA, 1637 Grand View Dr., spoke against Wrensmoor Castle and expressed
  concerns regarding traffic. He suggested that the operator needed to be present during events
  to enforce their rules and limit the number of events.

  8) Rich BROWERS, 1801 Alta Vista Dr., recalled past discussions regarding the use of the
  property, spoke against Wrensmoor, and discussed his thoughts on duplicitous attitude of Ms.
  Culver.

  9) David BAND spoke against Wrensmoor and discussed the negative impact on the
  neighborhood such as increased trash and general nuisances of a wedding and filming
  location.

  10) Pierre LAU, 1641 Grand View Dr., spoke against Wrensmoor and discussed the negative
  impact on the neighborhood such as noise, traffic, and general safety concerns.

  11) Frances R. VALDEZ, 1830 Alta Vista Dr., spoke against Wrensmoor and discussed the safety
  concerns of increased cars on narrow streets. She also discussed her concerns regarding
  coyotes in the neighborhood.

  2
12-9-24
   Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and Director of Community
  Development HO discussed traffic calming measures imposed by the City in the neighborhood
  such as red curbs, response from parking enforcement, and response from Code
  Enforcement. They also discussed the process to make a zone text amendment. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER noted that the City was informed that Wrensmoor had moved parking
  onto the property and expressed disappointment that that had not happened. She discussed
  the intent of the Short-Term Rental Ordinance to prevent such negative impacts and stated
  that there needed to be more improvements before a zoning change could be considered.

  Councilmember MALONEY emphasized that Council was providing direction this evening and
  not voting to change the zoning. He also discussed the Short-Term Rental Ordinance and
  echoed Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s comments that there needed to be improvements to address
  concerns. He suggested that there needed to be more conversations between the neighbors
  and the operators of Wrensmoor. He went on to discuss what the Conditional Use Permit
  (CUP) would entail and its enforcement. He also discussed the unique historic nature of the
  property and desire to preserve its character. He requested that Council direct staff to convene
  a conversation between Wrensmoor and neighbor representatives.

  Councilmember MAZA echoed Mr. Maloney’s statements concerning historic preservation of
  the property. He further emphasized that there should be zero burden on surrounding
  neighborhood and that any CUP would be temporary and that all impacts would have to be
  mitigated including noise, traffic, deliveries, and parking. He echoed Mr. Maloney’s concerns
  regarding the potential outcome of new ownership of the property and the changes that could
  be made despite the historic nature of the site.

  Vice Mayor LEE and Ms. CULVER discussed the concerns of the neighbors, the number of
  events that had taken place during the year, the number of planned events in 2025, and Ms.
  Culver’s presence at events. Ms. LEE further discussed the numerous complaints of the
  neighbors. She stated that she did not want to amend the zoning to allow for the operation of
  Wrensmoor and that she did not want to honor all scheduled events in 2025. She discussed
  the Short-Term Rental Ordinance and the concerns voiced by the neighbors at the meeting.

  Mr. MALONEY expressed that he felt there was a deal to be made between the operator and
  neighbors that was worth pursuing, adding that if an agreement could not be made that it would
  be acceptable. He motioned that Council direct staff to work with the interested parties to see
  if a compromise could be made. Mr. MAZA seconded the motion. Ms. LEE offered a friendly
  amendment to the motion, requesting that Mr. Ho be present for the meeting between 3
  representatives from the neighborhood, a representative from Code Enforcement, and Ms.
  Culver and that it take place before Christmas. Mr. MALONEY stated that he preferred for the
  community members to first meet with the operator and then determine to what degree staff
  involvement was necessary. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER offered to attend the meeting as well.
  City Attorney MONTES and Mr. MALONEY discussed the time constraints of scheduled City
  Council meetings and the winter holidays before the end of the calendar year. Mr. MALONEY
  amended his motion to direct the neighbors and operator meet on their own, that they then
  meet with staff and Ms. Andrade-Stadler, and that they in turn present a report of the meetings
  to Council at the January regular City Council meeting. Mr. MAZA seconded the motion.

  Action Taken:  City Council directed the neighborhood surrounding Wrensmoor
  Castle select representatives to meet with Wrensmoor operator, Cordelia Culver, regarding
  business operations, that that group would again meet with city staff and Councilmember
  Andrade-Stadler, and that staff present a report on the meeting to Council at the next regular
  City Council meeting. (M2M24-215)
  3
12-9-24
   Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, MALONEY, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 2 – 21)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda, with the exception of Item Nos. 9, 11, 17, and 19 were
considered by the City Council to be routine and were enacted by one motion.

2.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: JOSLYN CENTER FACILITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT –
F2M24-67, N2M24-147

  The City received $500,000 in congressionally directed grant funding from Representative
  Judy Chu for the Joslyn Senior Center Facility Improvement Project from the U.S. Department
  of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) Fiscal Year 2024 Economic Development Initiative
  (EDI) - Community Project Funding (CPF) grant. The exterior of the Joslyn Center needed
  new stucco and paint, cosmetic repairs, and a new roof. Specifications and bid documentation
  were completed and bids would be due no later than 10:30 a.m. on January 23, 2025 in the
  office of the City Clerk, and would be opened at 11:00 a.m. that same day.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken: City Council authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to prospective
  contractors for the Joslyn Center Facility Improvement Project; and, directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

3.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON CONCORD
  AVENUE AND MIDVALE PLACE – F2M24-68, N2M24-148

  The 4-inch cast iron water main on Concord Avenue between Winchester Avenue and
  Westboro Avenue and on Midvale Place between Winthrop Drive and Winchester Avenue
  were installed in 1923 and 1924 respectively. This segment of water main had a history of
  breaks, causing interruption of water service and damage to the road. Replacing the water
  main would greatly improve water flow, firefighting capabilities and overall system reliability.
  Plans and specifications were prepared. Staff reviewed the plans and found them to be
  consistent with the City’s standards.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Water Main Replacement Project on Concord Avenue and Midvale
  Place; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  4
12-9-24
   Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL CONSULTANT SERVICES FOR THE
  DEVELOPMENT OF THE FREMONT POCKET PARK PROJECT – F2M24-57,
  RFP2M24-18, C2M24-65, M2M24-205

  On August 26, 2024, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals for
  professional consultant services for the development of the Fremont Pocket Park Project
  (RFP2M24-18). On September 30, 2024, the City received seven proposals for professional
  consultant services for architecture and engineering services. Seven firms were invited to
  interview with City staff. The City’s consultant selection committee evaluated and ranked the
  consultants in accordance with criteria stated in the RFP, which included compliance with RFP
  requirements, project understanding, experience and level of effort, schedule, and cost-
  effectiveness to provide efficient services. The proposal received from Hirsch & Associates,
  Inc., was ranked highest.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Hirsch & Associates, Inc. in an amount not to exceed
  $123,750 for Professional Architecture and Engineering Services for the Fremont Pocket Park
  Project; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the City Council's
  action. (M2M24-205)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION
SERVICES FOR THE SEWER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON GLENAVEN AVENUE,
  ORANGE GROVE AVENUE, MIDWICK DRIVE, LA GOLONDRINA AVENUE AND ROSS
AVENUE – F2M24-64, RFP2M24-23, C2M24-66, M2M24-206

  On September 23, 2024, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals
  for professional engineering design services for the Sewer Replacement Project on Glenaven
  Avenue, Orange Grove Avenue, Midwick Drive, La Golondrina Avenue, and Ross Avenue
  (RFP2M24-23). As part of the City of Alhambra’s ongoing Capital Improvement Program, this
  project would provide engineering design, plans, and preparation of bid specifications for the
  replacement of approximately 2,525 feet of existing 12-inch sewer main with a larger capacity
  sewer main. Staff reviewed a total of four proposals. SA Associates was selected based on
  their distinguished qualifications, experience, reputation, responsiveness, availability, and
  cost.

  Discussion:  None.

  5
12-9-24
   Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and SA Associates
  for engineering design services for the Sewer Replacement Project on Glenhaven Avenue,
  Orange Grove Avenue, Midwick Drive, La Golondrina Avenue and Ross Avenue in an amount
  not to exceed $127,000; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M24-206)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  APPROVE CHANGE ORDER: WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT PROJECT ON
  MARENGO AVENUE – F2M24-34, C2M24-35, M2M24-208

  On May 13, 2024, the City Council awarded a contract to CEM Construction Corp. for the
  Water Main Replacement Project on Marengo Avenue in an amount not to exceed
  $659,105.00. During the final phase of construction, the contractor determined the existing
  water valves were not working properly for shut-off. The contractor could not abandon entire
  old pipe. However, about 20 feet of water line was still live and needed to be abandoned. The
  requested Change Order included not only abandoning the remaining water line, but also
  replacing 16-inch and 18-inch water valves and two Line Stops which were used for temporary
  shut-off of a section of pipe without disrupting service. Change Order No. 1 was previously
  approved for miscellaneous bid quantities adjustments in the amount of $15,577.43.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved Change Order No. 2 for the Water Main
  Replacement Project on Marengo Avenue, increasing Contract No. C2M24-35 with CEM
  Construction Corp. by $134,950.00 and bringing the total revised contract value to an amount
  not to exceed $809,632.43; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action. (M2M24-208)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT FOR TEMPORARY PLANNING AND STAFF SERVICES –
  F2M24-16, K2M24-383, M2M24-209

  The vacancy of a full-time Senior Planner position in October 2024 necessitated the
  Community Development Department's need to secure a temporary contract planner. On
  November 6, 2024, the City entered into a contract (K2M24-383) with Sagecrest Planning and
  Environmental to provide temporary staffing. The original contract was envisioned to provide
  immediate short-term staff support to fill a key position in the Division while the recruitment
  process began. Retaining the contract planner was vital to ensure acceptable service levels
  and minimize potential project delays; however, it was anticipated the recruitment process
  would take approximately six months.

  6
12-9-24
   Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract amendment, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and
  Sagecrest Planning and Environmental (K2M24-383), for temporary planning staffing services
  for an amount not to exceed $101,000; authorized the transfer of appropriations from salaries
  to temporary staffing services to cover the excess costs; and, directed staff to undertake the
  steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M24-209)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  FY 2023-2024 TO FY 2024-2025 CARRYOVERS - F2M23-17, F2M24-17, R2M24-49

  On June 26, 2023, the City Council adopted the Budget for Fiscal Years 2023/24 and 2024/25,
  which allocated funds to various departments and accounts within the City of Alhambra. On
  September 23, 2024, the City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-42, which approved
  budget carryovers and the reappropriation of outstanding encumbrances from Fiscal Year
  2023/24 to Fiscal Year 2024/25, at the close of Fiscal Year 2023/24. Due to an inadvertent
  oversight, the Police Department’s budget carryovers were not included in the prior resolution.
  These carryovers were essential to cover expenses related to delayed projects, specialized
  equipment, training, uniforms, and supplies. Staff requested the City Council approve
  Resolution No. R2M24-49, which included the necessary budget adjustments as outlined in
  the exhibit to the Resolution.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-49 entitled: A Resolution of
  the Alhambra City Council approving those certain fiscal year-end carryovers from fiscal year
  2023/24 to fiscal year 2024/25 at the close of the fiscal year 2023/24

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

9.  RESOLUTION APPROVING CHANGES TO THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA
  COMPENSATION PLAN AND SALARY SCHEDULE FOR PART-TIME JOB
  CLASSIFICATIONS – F2M24-2, R2M24-48, M2M24-207

  California Public Employees’ Retirement Law requires the City Council to approve and adopt
  salary schedules and pay rates for job classifications at a public meeting. Effective January 1,
  2025, the State of California Department of Industrial Relations Minimum Wage Order
  mandates that minimum wage for employers with 26 or more employees be increased from
  $16.00 per hour to $16.50 per hour. The proposed Resolution provided for increases for part-
  time hourly classifications to ensure compliance with the upcoming State of California

  7
12-9-24
   mandated minimum wage increase. To ensure compliance, the new part-time salary schedule
  shall be effective on the pay period beginning December 19, 2024.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St. suggested Council consider
  a higher salary for part-time positions.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER and City Manager BINNQUIST
  discussed the salary schedule.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M24-48 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council approving changes to the City of Alhambra Compensation Plan
  and Salary Schedule for part-time job classifications; and, directed the Finance Director to
  make necessary budget adjustments to comply with the State mandated minimum wage
  increase. (M2M24-207)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: FRONT STREET WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT AND ZONE
  CHANGE - PHASE 2 – F2M19-20, N2M24-150

  The City of Alhambra has two major pressure zones - the South Zone and North Zone. Mission
  Road is the dividing line between the two zones. Due to the pressure zone break, the residents
  along Front Street experienced low water pressure. Based on Hydraulic testing conducted in
  the area of Front Street between Marengo and Atlantic showed that moving the zone break
  south to Shorb Street and replacing the existing four-inch cast iron water mains would
  significantly increase the water pressure and fire flow capability in the area. The proposed
  project involved construction in three phases, sequentially over the next three years with one
  section of the project occurring each year. The first phase project on Front Street from Atlantic
  Boulevard to Olive Avenue was completed. This project was Phase 2, which would be on Front
  Street from Olive Avenue to Marengo, Benito Avenue from Front Street to Shorb Street, and
  on Cherry Lane east of Benito Street.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids to
  qualified contractors for the Front Street Water Main Replacement and Zone Change - Phase
  2 with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on January 9, 2025 and opened at 11:00 a.m. that
  same day; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

11.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: ALHAMBRA LIT CROSSWALK TRAFFIC CONTROL
  DEVICES PROJECT – F2M22-56, N2M24-151

  8
12-9-24
   The Alhambra Active Transportation Program (ATP), Lit Crosswalk Traffic Control Devices,
  SGV Measure M Subregional funding consists of improvements at the following locations:
  Main St./Meridian Ave.; Valley Blvd./Monterey St.; Main St./Marguerita Ave.; Chapel Ave./
  Elgin St.; Main St./Curtis Ave.; Valley Blvd./Date Ave.; Main St./Vega St.; Main St./Olive Ave.;
  and, Valley Blvd./Primrose Ave. The project design included the installation of pedestrian push
  button signals and signage at nine intersections that have an uncontrolled crosswalk.
  Pedestrian crossing control equipment at the intersections may include flashing beacons
  (standard beacons per CA-MUTCD or Rapid Rectangular Flashing Beacons (RRFB) or in-road
  flashing lights along crosswalk lines).

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., spoke regarding the need for
  pedestrian safety measures, particularly at Main St. and Cordova St. given the new Chinatown
  Service Center Care facility.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized the distribution of a Notice Inviting Bids for the
  Alhambra Lit Crosswalk Traffic Control Devices Project, with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m.
  on January 16, 2025; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the
  Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

12.  ACCEPTANCE OF 2023 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY GRANT – F2M15-25, M2M24-210

  Staff requested that the City Council approve an agreement with Los Angeles County and
  accept the 2023 State Homeland Security Grant Program (SHSGP). The Los Angeles
  Operational Area (OA) Approval Authority for the Homeland Security Grant Program
  established priorities for approval that focused on enhancing and expanding existing
  specialized resources that would improve the Operational Area’s ability to prepare for and
  respond to terrorism and weapons of mass destruction events, while providing an opportunity
  for cities to apply for funding to meet their needs. The Fire Department submitted a grant
  request in the amount of $5,200 for Urban Search and Rescue training.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken: City Council accepted the 2023 State Homeland Security Grant in the amount
  of $5,200 for the Fire Department; authorize the Fire Chief to sign the 2023 State Homeland
  Security Grant Program agreement with Los Angeles County, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney; appropriate revenues and expenditures in
  the amount of $5,200 for the 2024-25 Fiscal Year; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M24-210)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

  9
12-9-24
 13.  AWARD CONTRACT: BANKING SERVICES – F2M24-58, RFP2M24-19, C2M24-67,
M2M24-211

  The City of Alhambra banked with Bank of the West for over twenty years. However, following
  Bank of the West's acquisition by BMO Bank last year, the City experienced disruptions in
  banking services. In response, the City decided to issue a Request for Proposals (RFP) in
  order to secure a higher level of service and more competitive pricing for its banking needs.
  The goal was to ensure uninterrupted financial operations, including cash management and
  related services. On August 26, 2024, the City Council authorized the distribution of a RFP for
  professional banking services. The RFP was sent to qualified financial institutions on August
  27, 2024, and four firms submitted proposals. After reviewing the proposals based on technical
  qualifications and cost, U.S. Bank was selected as the most responsive proposer. U.S. Bank
  has over 100 years of experience serving government entities and managing over 5,800
  organizations. The contract would be for five years with a contract not to exceed amount of
  $210,000 and with an option to extend for up to ten additional years.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a five-year contract, subject to final language
  approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, to U.S. Bank for comprehensive banking
  services, with an option to extend the contract up to ten (10) additional one-year extensions at
  the City’s discretion in an amount not to exceed $210,000 for the initial 5-year term and
  $42,000 per year thereafter; directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize
  Council’s action; and, authorized the City Manager to execute the annual support agreements
  and extensions if services are satisfactory. (M2M24-211)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

14.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: ROOF REPLACEMENT AT THE UTILITIES CUSTOMER
  SERVICE CENTER – F2M24-69, N2M24-152

  The roof at the Utilities Customer Service Center had a built-up roofing system that was over
  15 years old. It was in need of constant repairs and it needed to be replaced. Specifications
  were prepared and would be included in the advertised Notice Inviting Bids.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to issue a Notice Inviting Bids for the roof
  replacement at the Customer Service Center, with bids due no later than 10:30 a.m. on
  January 9, 2025 and opened on 11:00 a.m. that same day; and, directed staff to undertake the
  steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MAZA, MALONEY, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE
